extracted.intended_audience: school and institutional Title IX compliance officers, higher-education administrators, legal counsel, and stakeholders participating in Title IX rulemaking or implementation
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble to final Title IX regulations describing statutory interpretation, procedural requirements, privacy obligations, and enforcement standards that recipients of Federal education funds must follow and that commenters should consider in notice-and-comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberate indifference — need to intensify response
rubrics_metrics.description: Even when a recipient's response to sex discrimination is assessed under the deliberate indifference standard in a private action for damages, some courts have recognized under certain circumstances that the recipient must take additional responsive action if its initial efforts to end sex discrimination are ineffective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If initial efforts 'have not sufficed' or harassment is ongoing/escalating, courts have required recipients to 'intensify, reassess, or adjust' their response rather than simply repeat ineffective measures. Examples: Cianciotto ex rel. D.S. v. NYC Dep't of Educ. (denying dismissal where officials failed to try something else) and Doe v. Sch. Dist. No. 1, Denver (reversing dismissal where pleading alleged officials knew actions had not sufficed).

rubrics_metrics.name: FERPA access to witness statements/video that cannot be segregated
rubrics_metrics.description: Under FERPA, a parent (or eligible student) has a right to inspect and review any witness statement that is directly related to the student, even if that statement contains information directly related to another student, if the information cannot be segregated and redacted without destroying its meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR has required disclosure where segregation/redaction would destroy meaning (example: surveillance video of a hazing incident provided to parents of disciplined student). Agencies should consider whether records can be redacted without destroying meaning before withholding under FERPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: When Title IX conflicts with FERPA, GEPA override applies
rubrics_metrics.description: When there is a direct conflict between the requirements of Title IX and FERPA, the GEPA override, as incorporated into § 106.6(e), applies such that a recipient must comply with Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By contrast, when there is a direct conflict between constitutional due process rights and FERPA, a constitutional override applies. The preamble refers readers to the detailed discussion of § 106.6(e) for interaction between FERPA and Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition/coverage of 'confidential employee' vs 'confidential resource'
rubrics_metrics.description: Some commenters used the term 'confidential resources' to encompass non-employees, but the term 'confidential employee' in the final regulations only covers employees of a recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble adopts 'confidential employee' as an employee-only category for regulatory purposes, while noting commenters' broader usage of 'confidential resources' in some submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients' responsibility to offer supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients have a responsibility for offering supportive measures to parties involved in sexual harassment/sex discrimination matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2020 amendments and the preamble discuss meaning of 'education program or activity,' the recipient's responsibility for offering supportive measures, and related duties; see discussion tied to § 106.44(a) and other sections for details on supportive measures' scope and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to follow grievance process before imposing sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient has a duty to follow the applicable grievance process before imposing any sanctions in response to allegations of sexual harassment/sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble notes this duty was part of § 106.44(a) of the 2020 amendments and is addressed elsewhere in the preamble; institutions should adhere to procedural steps in grievance processes prior to sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: FERPA: treatment records become education records if disclosed to student
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may choose to disclose a treatment record for a postsecondary student or a student who is eighteen years of age or older to that student, and that treatment record would then become an 'education record' under FERPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See U.S. Dep't of Educ., Dear Colleague Letter to School Officials (Aug. 2016) for explanation; institutions should account for this when deciding whether to disclose treatment records to students and the resulting FERPA obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy/confidentiality — limit disclosure of party identities
rubrics_metrics.description: In all cases, schools should make every effort to prevent disclosure of the names of all parties involved, the complainant, the witnesses, and the accused, except to the extent necessary to carry out an investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard (from 2001 Revised Sexual Harassment Guidance) emphasizes minimizing identifying disclosures; agencies/institutions should restrict disclosures to what is necessary for investigation and resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speak Out Act — nondisclosure clauses unenforceable pre-dispute
rubrics_metrics.description: The Speak Out Act generally prohibits the judicial enforceability of a nondisclosure clause or non-disparagement clause before a dispute arises involving a sexual assault or sexual harassment alleged to be in violation of Federal, State, or tribal law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions and parties should not rely on NDAs/non-disparagement provisions to prevent later judicial enforcement when the subject is sexual assault/harassment; the preamble cites 42 U.S.C. 19403.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministerial exception not generally extended to student organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Although some courts have applied the ministerial exception to protect rights of religious student organizations, other courts have rejected extending the ministerial exception to disputes regarding student organizations; the ministerial exception is an affirmative defense grounded in the First Amendment that precludes application of employment discrimination laws to employment relationships between religious institutions and their members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should not assume ministerial-exception protections apply to student-organization disputes; case law is split and the Department notes courts' rejections of such extensions (e.g., InterVarsity v. Univ. of Iowa).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology choice — prefer 'sexual interests' over 'sexual predisposition'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department views the term 'sexual interests' as more appropriate than the term 'sexual predisposition,' which the Department views as an outdated phrase that may conjure assumptions it seeks to prohibit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble uses 'sexual predisposition' only when referencing the 2020 amendments' requirements; agencies and institutions should use terminology that avoids stigmatizing or outdated language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy and related conditions — definition and interchangeable phrasing
rubrics_metrics.description: The preamble uses the terms 'pregnancy or related conditions' and 'pregnant or experiencing pregnancy-related conditions' interchangeably to mean any condition covered under the definition of 'pregnancy or related conditions' in final § 106.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory text relies on § 106.2 definition; institutions should treat the interchangeable phrasing as covering the full scope of conditions defined there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy Discrimination Act (PDA) and lactation — coverage not limited to incapacitating conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Some courts have read PDA protection of pregnancy-related medical conditions to require the conditions be 'incapacitating,' but EEOC guidance disagrees; the Department agrees with courts (e.g., Fifth Circuit) that the PDA contains no such limitation and that lactation is a pregnancy-related medical condition covered under the PDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should recognize lactation/breastfeeding as protected pregnancy-related conditions under the PDA and not condition protections on incapacitation; see cases like Hicks v. City of Tuscaloosa and EEOC Enforcement Guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental fairness in disciplinary proceedings; limited right to counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: In private-school disciplinary procedures courts generally have required adherence to a standard of 'fundamental' or 'basic' fairness, but there is generally no right to counsel in disciplinary proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some courts (and commenters) have argued for cross-examination rights in certain contexts; the Department notes that requirements vary by court and by whether constitutional protections apply. See Haidak (no general right to counsel) and discussion of cases requiring cross-examination in some state-court contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice-and-comment timing — 30 days generally shortest for substantial rule changes
rubrics_metrics.description: When substantial rule changes are proposed, a 30-day comment period is generally the shortest time period sufficient for interested persons to meaningfully review a proposed rule and provide informed comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited case law (Nat'l Lifeline Ass'n v. FCC) supports that agencies should allow at least 30 days for comment on substantial changes; rulewriters should consider longer periods for complex or far-reaching proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction of Title IX with other civil-rights statutes
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in Title IX's chapter shall be construed to affect the applicability of title VI, title V of the Rehabilitation Act, the Age Discrimination Act, or other statutes prohibiting discrimination, to any applicable program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must remain mindful of overlapping obligations under multiple civil-rights statutes; compliance with Title IX does not relieve obligations under other federal nondiscrimination laws.
